annotations.text:
SHIPPED

D4, built and installed. The app no longer runs on the stock Android robot.

The R is the real Inter Tight ExtraBold outline pulled from the vendored TTF — not live text, not traced by eye. Everything on this board renders from the committed XML.

ONE NUMBER WORTH KNOWING

The letter height (46 units) was solved, not chosen: it is the largest letter whose ink-box corner stays inside the mask with 4 units of parallax headroom.

The first attempt was 52 and its corners sat at 33.49 against a 36 limit — fine at rest, grazed under parallax. That would have shown up on a Pixel, not here.

THE ONE FRAGILE THING

VectorDrawable has no mask element, so the gap is cut by drawing the letter TWICE — clipped above, clipped below.

Edit one group without the other and the mark silently desyncs. build_icon.py regenerates both from one constant; use it rather than hand-editing.

WHY 6 → 5.3

The gap was picked at 24dp, where it renders ~1.2px — the smallest cut that still reads rather than looking like a rendering fault.

These tiles were drawn at the earlier 52-unit letter height. When the letter came down to 46 for parallax headroom, the gap scaled with it to keep the same optical proportion.

One drawing, all sizes — no optical-size variant to keep in sync.

YOU PICKED: MONOGRAM

"I like monogram better but it kind of looks ugly."

Agreed — and the direction was not the problem. A default glyph dropped into a coloured square is the laziest form this idea takes, and that is what D was.

So the style is held fixed here. Only the letterform, the crop and the idea vary.

THE AXES

D1 fixes the execution, nothing more — the control.

D2 changes the TYPEFACE (serif, bookish).
D3 changes the CROP (bleed off-edge).
D4 changes the IDEA (the letter, partly forgotten).
D5 changes the CONTAINER (the cloze blank).
D6 changes the FIGURE/GROUND (knockout on dark).

One variable each, so a preference tells you something.

IF YOU WANT A RECOMMENDATION

D4. It is the only one that is still a monogram — simple, legible, yours — while also being about something. A letter your eye has to complete is the product in one image.

Its one real problem is small sizes, and that is solvable: ship a wider gap below 32dp, the way icon families normally carry an optical-size variant.

D2 is the safer pick if you want handsome over clever.

STILL JUDGE IT AT 24dp

Same as last time: the small row is where these separate. Squint at it, or step back from the screen.

D1 and D2 hold. D4's gap narrows to a hairline. D5 goes busy. D3 depends entirely on the mask shape.

A launcher icon is seen small and in a hurry far more often than it is seen like this.

NOT DECIDED YET

These are drawn with live text so they were quick to iterate. The moment you pick one, the glyph gets converted to outlines and hand-corrected as a path — a shipped icon must never depend on a font being present or on a renderer's hinting.

That conversion is also where the optical corrections happen properly.

SUPERSEDED — kept for reference

The first pass: four directions across the whole space (Spine, Cloze blank, Recall curve, Monogram).

Monogram was picked. The other three stay here in case a later look changes your mind.
